# CivilKit Buckling (CUFSM): the analysis on screen, as a script for cufsm-rs-py
#   pip install cufsm-rs-py
# The model is the page's own, table for table (CUFSM's prop, node and elem, numbered from 1).
# Units: the model's own consistent set (the page labels lengths mm and stresses MPa).
import cufsm_rs

prop = [  # mat#, Ex, Ey, vx, vy, G
    [100, 200000, 200000, 0.3, 0.3, 76923.0769231],
]
node = [  # node#, x, z, xdof, zdof, ydof, qdof, stress
    [1, 60, 40, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
    [2, 60, 30, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
    [3, 60, 20, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
    [4, 60, 10, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
    [5, 60, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
    [6, 45, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
    [7, 30, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
    [8, 15, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
    [9, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
    [10, 0, 37.5, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
    [11, 0, 75, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
    [12, 0, 112.5, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
    [13, 0, 150, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
    [14, 15, 150, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
    [15, 30, 150, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
    [16, 45, 150, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
    [17, 60, 150, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
    [18, 60, 140, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
    [19, 60, 130, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
    [20, 60, 120, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
    [21, 60, 110, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
]
elem = [  # elem#, nodei, nodej, t, mat#
    [1, 1, 2, 1.5, 100],
    [2, 2, 3, 1.5, 100],
    [3, 3, 4, 1.5, 100],
    [4, 4, 5, 1.5, 100],
    [5, 5, 6, 1.5, 100],
    [6, 6, 7, 1.5, 100],
    [7, 7, 8, 1.5, 100],
    [8, 8, 9, 1.5, 100],
    [9, 9, 10, 1.5, 100],
    [10, 10, 11, 1.5, 100],
    [11, 11, 12, 1.5, 100],
    [12, 12, 13, 1.5, 100],
    [13, 13, 14, 1.5, 100],
    [14, 14, 15, 1.5, 100],
    [15, 15, 16, 1.5, 100],
    [16, 16, 17, 1.5, 100],
    [17, 17, 18, 1.5, 100],
    [18, 18, 19, 1.5, 100],
    [19, 19, 20, 1.5, 100],
    [20, 20, 21, 1.5, 100],
]
springs = []  # #, nodei, nodej (0 = ground), ku, kv, kw, kq, local, discrete, ys
constraints = []  # node#e, dofe, coeff, node#k, dofk
model = cufsm_rs.Model(prop=prop, node=node, elem=elem,
                       springs=springs or None, constraints=constraints or None)

# the 12 physical lengths from the page's length list
lengths = [100, 142.70914972418177, 203.65901414998953, 290.6400474301011, 414.76994044545637, 591.9146553212059, 844.7163717017144, 1205.4875516364755, 1720.3410349712726, 2455.0840633636944, 3503.62959184022, 4999.999999999999]
res = cufsm_rs.strip(model, lengths, m_all=3, bc="C-C", neigs=1)   # terms 1..3 at every length
lf = list(res.curve)   # the lowest load factor at each length


def minima(L, f):
    """The page's minima: every interior local minimum, a still-falling last point, and for a
    curve with neither, its lowest point."""
    out = [i for i in range(1, len(f) - 1) if f[i] <= f[i - 1] and f[i] < f[i + 1]]
    if len(f) > 1 and f[-1] < f[-2]:
        out.append(len(f) - 1)
    if not out:
        out = [min(range(len(f)), key=lambda i: f[i])]
    return [(L[i], f[i]) for i in out]


ref = max(abs(n[7]) for n in node)   # the reference stress: the largest nodal stress
for L, f in minima(lengths, lf):
    print(f"L = {L:.6g} mm   load factor {f:.12g}   sigma_cr = {f * ref:.6g} MPa")

# CivilKit Buckling (CUFSM): the analysis on screen, as a script for cufsm-rs-py
#   pip install cufsm-rs-py
# The model is the page's own, table for table (CUFSM's prop, node and elem, numbered from 1).
# Units: the model's own consistent set (the page labels lengths mm and stresses MPa).
import cufsm_rs

prop = [  # mat#, Ex, Ey, vx, vy, G
    [100, 29500, 29500, 0.3, 0.3, 11346.15],
]
node = [  # node#, x, z, xdof, zdof, ydof, qdof, stress
    [1, 5, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, -38.889],
    [2, 5, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, -50],
    [3, 2.5, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, -50],
    [4, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, -50],
    [5, 0, 3, 1, 1, 1, 1, -16.667],
    [6, 0, 6, 1, 1, 1, 1, 16.667],
    [7, 0, 9, 1, 1, 1, 1, 50],
    [8, 2.5, 9, 1, 1, 1, 1, 50],
    [9, 5, 9, 1, 1, 1, 1, 50],
    [10, 5, 8, 1, 1, 1, 1, 38.889],
]
elem = [  # elem#, nodei, nodej, t, mat#
    [1, 1, 2, 0.1, 100],
    [2, 2, 3, 0.1, 100],
    [3, 3, 4, 0.1, 100],
    [4, 4, 5, 0.1, 100],
    [5, 5, 6, 0.1, 100],
    [6, 6, 7, 0.1, 100],
    [7, 7, 8, 0.1, 100],
    [8, 8, 9, 0.1, 100],
    [9, 9, 10, 0.1, 100],
]
springs = [  # #, nodei, nodej (0 = ground), ku, kv, kw, kq, local, discrete, ys
    [1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 5, 0, 1, 0, 0],

constraints = [  # node#e, dofe, coeff, node#k, dofk
    [10, 2, 1, 1, 2],
]
model = cufsm_rs.Model(prop=prop, node=node, elem=elem,
                       springs=springs or None, constraints=constraints or None)

# the 40 half-wavelengths from the page's length list
lengths = [1, 1.1937766417144364, 1.425102670302998, 1.701254279852589, 2.0309176209047357, 2.4244620170823286, 2.8942661247167507, 3.455107294592219, 4.1246263829013525, 4.923882631706739, 5.878016072274914, 7.017038286703828, 8.37677640068292, 10, 11.937766417144363, 14.251026703029979, 17.012542798525892, 20.309176209047358, 24.244620170823282, 28.942661247167504, 34.5510729459222, 41.24626382901352, 49.23882631706739, 58.780160722749116, 70.1703828670383, 83.7677640068292, 100, 119.3776641714437, 142.5102670302998, 170.1254279852589, 203.09176209047348, 242.44620170823282, 289.4266124716752, 345.5107294592218, 412.4626382901352, 492.3882631706742, 587.8016072274912, 701.7038286703829, 837.6776400682916, 1000]
res = cufsm_rs.signature(model, lengths)   # S-S, one half-wave at each half-wavelength
lf = list(res.curve)   # the lowest load factor at each length


def minima(L, f):
    """The page's minima: every interior local minimum, a still-falling last point, and for a
    curve with neither, its lowest point."""
    out = [i for i in range(1, len(f) - 1) if f[i] <= f[i - 1] and f[i] < f[i + 1]]
    if len(f) > 1 and f[-1] < f[-2]:
        out.append(len(f) - 1)
    if not out:
        out = [min(range(len(f)), key=lambda i: f[i])]
    return [(L[i], f[i]) for i in out]


ref = max(abs(n[7]) for n in node)   # the reference stress: the largest nodal stress
for L, f in minima(lengths, lf):
    print(f"L = {L:.6g} mm   load factor {f:.12g}   sigma_cr = {f * ref:.6g} MPa")

import cufsm_rs as fsm

# CUFSM's tutorial C: 9 x 5 x 1 in, t = 0.1 in (inches and ksi)
xz = [(5, 1), (5, 0), (2.5, 0), (0, 0), (0, 3), (0, 6), (0, 9), (2.5, 9), (5, 9), (5, 8)]
m = fsm.Model(
    prop=[[100, 29500, 29500, 0.3, 0.3, 11346.15]],
    node=[[i + 1, x, z, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0] for i, (x, z) in enumerate(xz)],
    elem=[[i + 1, i + 1, i + 2, 0.1, 100] for i in range(9)],
)

p = fsm.section_properties(m)          # p.A, p.Ixx, p.J, p.Cw, p.xs, ... (also p["Ixx"])
y = fsm.first_yield(m, fy=50)          # y.Py = 105, y.Mxx = 324.64 (element faces, as CUFSM)

mc = fsm.stress(m, P=y.Py)             # a new Model with the reference stresses set
sig = fsm.signature(mc, [10 ** (3 * i / 79) for i in range(80)])
sig                                    # StripResult(signature, bc=S-S, 80 lengths 1 to 1000, neigs=1, 2 minima)
sig.minima                             # [[7.27, 0.353], [43.9, 0.544]]: [half-wavelength, load factor]
sig.classify_minima()                  # [G, D, L, O] percent of each minimum's mode: L 98%, D 94%

r = fsm.strip(mc, [7.27, 43.9], neigs=3)   # any lengths, several modes
r.load_factors                             # (2, 3)
shape = r.mode_shape(0)                    # the lowest mode at the first length
shape.u, shape.v, shape.w, shape.theta     # each (terms, nodes)
shape.dofs                                 # the raw vector, CUFSM's DOF order
shape.at()                                 # displacements summed over terms at mid-length

dist = fsm.strip(mc, [43.9], spaces="D", neigs=1)                  # pure distortional (cFSM)
cc = fsm.strip(mc, [100.0, 200.0], m_all=10, bc="C-C", neigs=2)    # general end conditions
cc.classify()                                                       # (2, 2, 4): G, D, L, O percent

lc = fsm.lipped_c(200, 76, 15, 1.9, ri=3)    # mm; 37 nodes
